title: The 8.75% capital ratio in the RRC formula currently has no effect, because it appears once as a divisor and once as a multiplier
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.5 specifies the final step of the lending-market capital calculation as `RRC = K × (1/CR) × EAD × ECR`, where `CR` is "the capital ratio without additional buffers" set to 8.75% and `ECR` is "the capital ratio included additional capital buffers established by Sky Governance." A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.5.3 then states: "There are currently no additional capital buffers so the ECR is equal to the CR, which is 8.75%."

When ECR = CR the two terms cancel exactly, and RRC is simply the Basel capital requirement K times exposure at default. The reference implementation confirms this reading: its final line is `rrc = credit_risk * ead`, with no capital ratio appearing anywhere.

So the 8.75% figure — the most recognizably Basel-flavoured number in the Article — is currently inert. It is not a scaling factor on required capital; it is a *placeholder denominator* whose only function is to give governance a lever. Setting ECR above CR raises requirements by the ratio ECR/CR, uniformly, across every lending-market Instance at once.

This is worth recording because the formula reads as though a capital-ratio calibration is doing work when it is not. Anyone reasoning about how conservative the framework is should look at K (which embeds the 99.9% quantile and the 0.13/0.33 correlation bounds), not at 8.75%. And anyone wanting to tighten the framework system-wide has exactly one dial that does not require re-deriving any model: the ECR/CR spread.
description: RRC = K × (1/CR) × EAD × ECR, and ECR equals CR while no buffers exist — so the terms cancel and the reference implementation correctly reduces to RRC = credit risk × EAD.
